summary: This note is a compiled excerpt from the Wikipedia article on the Korean War, covering the military strength of North Korean forces in 1950, the origins of the division of Korea, the outbreak of war on 25 June 1950, UN and Chinese intervention, the Chinese New Year's Offensive, and the protracted armistice negotiations ending in July 1953. It also covers the Soviet and Chinese roles, Japanese colonial rule and wartime exploitation of Korea, and the U.S. and UN rationale for intervention. The text contains some repeated paragraphs and conflicting accounts, which the note presents as historians' claims.
one_line: Wikipedia-derived overview of the Korean War's 1950-1953 origins, opening campaigns, Chinese intervention, and armistice talks.
key_facts: By mid-1950, North Korean forces numbered between 150,000 and 200,000 troops, organized into 10 infantry divisions, one tank division, and one air force division.
North Korean forces on the eve of the invasion included 274 T-34-85 tanks and 200 artillery pieces.
North Korean forces moved into South Korea on 25 June 1950.
On 27 June 1950, the United Nations Security Council adopted S/RES/83 and decided the formation and dispatch of UN Forces in Korea.
Twenty-one countries of the United Nations eventually contributed to the defense of South Korea, with the United States providing 88% of the UN's military personnel.
On 27 June 1950, President Truman dispatched the United States Seventh Fleet to the Taiwan Strait.
On 8 October 1950, Mao Zedong redesignated the PLA North East Frontier Force as the Chinese People's Volunteer Army (PVA).
On 15 October 1950, President Truman and General MacArthur met at Wake Island in the mid-Pacific Ocean.
In the Battle of Unsan on 1 November 1950, PVA 39th Army soldiers encircled and attacked the U.S. 8th Cavalry Regiment.
The Chinese New Year's Offensive began on New Year's Eve of 1950 and allowed the PVA and KPA to conquer Seoul for the second time on 4 January 1951.
Armistice negotiations began on 10 July 1951 at Kaesong and the final armistice agreement was signed on 27 July 1953.
Stalin gave Kim permission to invade the South in April 1950, on condition that Mao would agree to send reinforcements if needed.
On 1 October 1946, Korean police killed three students in the Daegu Uprising, and protesters then killed 38 policemen.
Japanese forces in Korea increased from 46,000 soldiers in 1941 to 300,000 in 1945.
Truman described the war as a 'police action' because the United States never formally declared war on its opponents.

entities.name: Kim Il-sung
entities.role: North Korean leader who planned and launched the invasion of South Korea

entities.name: Mao Zedong
entities.role: Chinese leader who agreed to support the North Korean invasion and redesignated the PLA North East Frontier Force as the PVA

entities.name: Zhou Enlai
entities.role: Chinese leader who warned the United States that China was prepared to intervene and directed the Chinese peace talks

entities.name: Stalin
entities.role: Soviet leader who gave Kim permission to invade the South under conditions

entities.name: Syngman Rhee
entities.role: South Korean leader elected president on 20 July 1948 and rejected North Korean peace overtures

entities.name: Harry S. Truman
entities.role: U.S. President who dispatched the Seventh Fleet to the Taiwan Strait and ordered U.S. air and sea forces to help South Korea

entities.name: MacArthur
entities.role: U.S. General who met Truman at Wake Island on 15 October 1950

entities.name: Peng Dehuai
entities.role: Chinese commander appointed to lead Chinese forces in Korea

entities.name: Lin Biao
entities.role: Chinese leader who refused Mao's offer to command Chinese forces in Korea, citing medical treatment

entities.name: Matthew Ridgway
entities.role: U.S. General who assumed command of the U.S. Eighth Army on 26 December and ordered Operation Roundup

entities.name: Bruce Cumings
entities.role: Historian who argued the KPA's rapid withdrawal was strategic

entities.name: K. S. Thimayya
entities.role: Indian General who chaired the Neutral Nations Repatriation Commission

entities.name: Chiang Kai-shek
entities.role: Nationalist leader whose Encirclement Campaigns Chinese communist forces escaped in the 1930s

entities.name: Korean People's Army
entities.role: North Korean armed force that crossed the 38th parallel on 25 June 1950

entities.name: People's Volunteer Army
entities.role: Chinese force redesignated on 8 October 1950 from the PLA North East Frontier Force

entities.name: United Nations Security Council
entities.role: body that condemned the North Korean invasion and authorized UN forces via Resolution 82 and 83

entities.name: United States Seventh Fleet
entities.role: naval force Truman dispatched to the Taiwan Strait on 27 June 1950

entities.name: Soviet Advisory Group
entities.role: Soviet generals sent to North Korea who completed the attack plans by May 1950

entities.name: Daegu Uprising
entities.role: 1946 protest in which Korean police killed three students and protesters killed 38 policemen

entities.name: Battle of Unsan
entities.role: 1 November 1950 Chinese surprise assault on the U.S. 8th Cavalry Regiment

entities.name: Chinese New Year's Offensive
entities.role: PVA and KPA Third Phase Offensive launched on New Year's Eve of 1950

entities.name: Wake Island
entities.role: mid-Pacific site of the Truman and MacArthur meeting on 15 October 1950

entities.name: Kaesong
entities.role: city where armistice negotiations began on 10 July 1951

entities.name: Panmunjom
entities.role: neighbouring village where armistice negotiations continued after Kaesong

entities.name: Pusan perimeter
entities.role: area enclosed by the UN Command by September 1950, about 10% of Korea
